spine.deviation_notes: The 'ground-lying weapons ARE the summon ammunition; the loot drop-stream is the resource pool' is the kit's signature identity and has no engine lane — engine proxies draw from mana/corpses, not consumed ground-item entities. Mapped as a standard transient poison-proxy swarm (PROXY_FISSION) which captures the combat feel but LOSES the loot-becomes-ammo resource-substrate. A player of the original would miss that their army's size and cadence were fed by what dropped on the floor. Docket candidate filed.

skills.delivery_notes: rains a volley of blades that linger on the ground; in engine terms a multi_projectile placement that seeds the summon source — the lingering blades are the ammunition substrate

animates each lingering blade into a transient ranged sword-minion (proxy) that fires projectiles dealing poison; the proxy is the dominant every-3-seconds damage source. totem geometry = placed autonomous proxy entity

mapping_json.motion_frame: kite-and-seed caster: drop blades, animate the swarm, reposition while transient ranged proxies poison the pack

economy: summon-cadence (low re-summon frequency in maps; long proxy duration)

mapping_json.fidelity_notes: Element: base skill is physical but the meta variant (Ranged Arms) is a POISON minion build; poison here is a necromancer/corruption register -> shadow family + poison ailment lane (crosswalk §1 poison-row: shadow when corruption-themed, minions=necro). Geometry: the animated weapons are transient proxies (totem geometry = placed autonomous entity); Bladefall is the multi_projectile feeder. PROXY_FISSION routes 'one summoning action -> many transient proxies'. THE MISSED IDENTITY: 'loot lying on the ground literally becomes ammunition; the drop stream is the resource pool' — engine proxies summon from mana/corpses, NOT from ground-dropped item entities. That resource-substrate (ground-item-consumption-as-summon-fuel) has no engine lane; docketed. A Poison-Ranged-AW player would notice their summons are no longer gated by/fed from the loot-drop stream — the flavor that made this kit iconic.
